questions.sampleAnswer: The Siberian Traps were formed by massive outpouring of lava over millions of years. These eruptions produced huge amounts of SO2 and CO2. questions.stem:
Evaluate the effectiveness of planting native trees in solving problems studied in the Earth and Environmental Science course. Support your answer with TWO specific, unrelated examples.
Examples may include:
• natural disasters
• resource management problems
• climate related problems
• other environmental problems.

criteria.text: Demonstrates extensive knowledge and understanding of TWO problems to explain how planting native trees can solve identified problems ; Makes clearly supported judgements based on criteria
Demonstrates thorough knowledge and understanding of TWO problems to explain how planting native trees can solve identified problems ; Makes a supported judgement based on criteria
Demonstrates sound knowledge and understanding of how planting trees can solve problem(s) ; Makes a judgement
Demonstrates basic knowledge and understanding of the benefits of trees OR Outlines relevant environmental problem(s)
Provides some relevant information

questions.sampleAnswer: Anthropogenic climate change is caused by activities such as burning coal to generate electricity, which introduces excess CO2 into the atmosphere. CO2 traps the Sun’s heat causing global warming. As native trees grow, they photosynthesise, capturing CO2 from the atmosphere and locking the carbon in their wood. Trees draw water from the soil by transpiration, which draws heat from surrounding air to evaporate water from the tree’s leaves. This cools the air around the tree, reducing local warmer temperatures. Mines produce large quantities of tailings, waste material which can escape causing dust pollution in the air and contaminating waterways. Tailings are stored in dams. During mine reclamation the tailings dam is covered in topsoil and trees are planted over the dam. Tree roots stabilise the soil, which contains the tailings by preventing erosion. Choosing native trees also provides habitat. Planting deep rooted native trees is very effective in combating climate change because they capture CO2, act as a carbon sink and lower local temperatures. Trees successfully contain mine tailings protecting the surrounding environment.

Outlines an effect humans have on a water resource

questions.sampleAnswer: Sustainability involves meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs. Pollution is a human activity that adds litter and chemicals to waterways, such as microplastics, agricultural run-off or oils from transport. This negatively impacts the sustainability of water as a resource as it blocks waterways and reduces water quality for aquatic organisms. The reduction in water quality makes the water unsafe for humans to use in the future. Off-creek water storage dams, where water is taken from rivers during high-flow with good quality and stored for future use is a very sustainable practice. This ensures water-flow and quality in rivers during times of drought, whilst meeting the needs of a community for access to water.
